author_scope.title: 特殊情况：线性阵列的奇异性处理
author_scope.takeaway: 当传感器共线时，常规矩阵奇异失效。本文通过变量代换$w = x + ay$将问题降维，导出一个关于$y$的二次方程，获得与经典解一致的显式闭式解，证明了方法在退化几何下的有效性。
author_scope.interaction: 几何切换器：用户将传感器布局从‘任意分布’切换为‘线性排列’，界面提示常规矩阵求逆失败（显示红色警告），随后自动展示变量代换过程及最终的一元二次方程解法。
author_scope.changes: 改变传感器几何构型，观察求解策略从‘两步加权最小二乘’自动切换为‘变量代换 + 二次方程求解’的路径变化。
author_scope.acceptance: 用户能说明线性阵列导致矩阵奇异的原因，以及本文通过引入中间变量$w$解决该问题的具体代数手段。

art_direction: 采用‘精密工程蓝图’风格。背景为浅灰白色研究台面，核心视觉元素为深蓝色（#2c3e50）的几何线条与淡青色（#a8dadc）的高亮数据流。公式推导过程以‘透明图层’形式叠加在几何示意图上，强调代数变换的透明度。图表部分保留原始数据的严谨性，使用深红（#e74c3c）标记性能拐点（阈值效应）。不使用装饰性图标，所有视觉焦点集中在‘非线性转线性’的几何变换与误差协方差椭圆的收缩过程。

nodes.title: 特殊情况：线性阵列几何中的奇异性处理
nodes.summary: 当传感器呈线性排列时，常规解法中的矩阵会因秩亏（singular）而失效。本文通过重写方程，将问题转化为关于新变量 w = x + ay 的线性系统，从而避免求逆失败。该方法在特定坐标系下可简化为与 Abel & Smith [4] 相同的闭式解，证明了其在退化几何下的有效性。
paragraphs: 在双曲定位的一般公式中，若传感器坐标满足线性关系 yi = axi + b，则包含位置信息的矩阵将变为奇异矩阵（singular），导致无法直接求逆求解（R00003, R00004）。
为解决此问题，作者将原方程重写为关于变量 w = x + ay 和 T1 的线性方程组（Eq. 27）。由于这两个变量相互独立，第一阶段过程可直接给出解，无需第二阶段修正（R00005, R00006）。
得到 w 和 T1 后，将其代入距离方程（Eq. 5），可导出一个关于 y 的一元二次方程。解出 y 后，利用 x = w - ay 即可恢复 x 坐标（R00007, R00008）。
若阵列位于 x 轴且第一个传感器在原点（a=b=0），该解进一步简化为 y = sqrt(...) 和 x = w 的形式。作者指出，此结果与文献 [4] 中给出的最优解完全一致（R00009）。
对于协方差分析，通过对随机量进行扰动推导，证明了在线性阵列情况下，该估计量的协方差矩阵与 CRLB（克拉美 - 罗下界）一致，表明其在该特殊构型下也是渐进有效的（R00033, R00035）。

claims.statement: 当传感器呈线性排列时，常规方法中的矩阵因秩亏而奇异，无法直接求解。
conditions: 传感器坐标满足 yi = axi + b

claims.statement: 通过引入中间变量 w = x + ay，可将非线性问题转化为线性系统求解，并最终通过解二次方程获得位置估计。
在阵列位于 x 轴的特殊情况下，本文推导的解与 Abel & Smith [4] 提出的最优解形式完全相同。
conditions: 第一个传感器位于原点

steps.title: 步骤 1：识别奇异性
steps.text: 检查传感器坐标是否满足线性关系 yi = axi + b。若满足，常规矩阵求逆失效。

steps.title: 步骤 2：变量代换
steps.text: 定义新变量 w = x + ay，将原方程组重写为关于 w 和 T1 的线性方程（Eq. 27）。

steps.title: 步骤 3：求解二次方程
steps.text: 利用求得的 w 和 T1，代入距离约束方程，构建关于 y 的二次方程并求解，进而反推 x。

assumptions: 传感器位置精确已知（或不确定性已纳入权重矩阵）
TDOA 测量误差较小，使得线性化近似有效
噪声协方差矩阵 Q 已知或可估计

S005.quote:
Abstract-An 
effective technique in locating a source based on 
intersections of hyperbolic curves defined by the time differences 
of arrival of a signal received at a number of sensors is proposed. 
The approach is noniterative and gives au explicit solution. It is 
an approximate realization of the maximum-likelihood estimator 
and is shown to attain the Cramer-Rao lower bound near the 
small error region. Comparisons of performance with existing 
techniques of beamformer, sphericat-interpolation, divide and 
conquer, and iterative Taylor-series methods are made. The 
proposed technique performs significantly better than spherical- 
interpolation, and has a higher noise threshold than divide and 
conquer before performance breaks away from the Cramer-Rao 
lower bound. It provides an explicit solution form that is not 
available in the beamformmg and Taylor-series methods. Compu- 
tational complexity is comparable to spherical-interpolation but 
substantially less than the Taylor-series method.

S007.quote:
N sonar and radar, it is often of interest to determine the 
I 
location of an object from its emissions [l]. A number 
of spatially separated sensors capture the emitted signal and 
the time differences of arrival (TDOA’s) at the sensors are 
determined. Using the TDOA’s, emitter location relative to 
the sensors can be calculated.

S008.quote:
The position fix is simplified when the sensors are arranged 
in a linear fashion. Many optimum processing techniques 
have been proposed, with different complexity and restrictions. 
Carter’s focused beamforming [l] requires a search over a set 
of possible source locations. Hahn’s method [2]-[3] assumes a 
distant source. Abel and Smith [4] provide an explicit solution 
that can achieve the Cram&-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) in the 
small error region.

S009.quote:
The situation is more complex when sensors are distributed 
arbitrarily. In this case, emitter position is determined from the 
intersection of a set of hyperbolic curves defined by the TDOA 
estimates. Finding the solution is not easy as the equations are 
nonlinear. Fang [5] gave an exact solution when the number of 
TDOA measurements are equal to the number of unknowns 
(coordinates of transmitter). This solution, however, cannot 
make use of extra measurements, available when there are 
extra sensors, to improve position accuracy. The more general 
situation with extra measurements was considered by Friedlan-

Although closed-form solutions have been developed, their 
estimators are not optimum. The divide and conquer (DAC) 
method [ 101 from Abel can achieve optimum performance, but 
it requires that the Fisher information is sufficiently large. To 
obtain a precise position estimate at reasonable noise levels, 
the Taylor-series method [ 113-[ 121 is commonly employed. 
It is an iterative method: it starts with an initial guess and 
improves the estimate at each step by determining. the local 
linear least-squares (LS) solution. An initial guess close to 
the true solution is needed to avoid local minima. Selection 
of such a starting point is not simple in practice. Moreover, 
convergence of the iterative process is not assured. It is also 
computationally intensive as LS computation is required in 
each iteration.

S014.quote:
We give an alternative solution for hyperbolic position fix. 
The solution is in closed-form, valid for both distant and close 
sources, and is an approximation of the maximum likelihood 
(ML) estimator when the TDOA estimation errors are small. 
To illustrate, Section I1 considers a 2-D localization problem 
with an arbitrary array manifold. In the special case of a linear 
array, the solution reduces to the one given by [4]. With three 
sensors to provide two TDOA estimates, an exact solution is 
obtained which is equivalent to the result in [7]. With four 
or more sensors, the original set of TDOA equations are 
transformed into another set of equations which are linear 
in source position coordinates and an extra variable. The 
weighted linear LS gives an initial solution. A second weighted 
LS, which makes use of the known constraint between source 
coordinates and the extra variable, gives an improved position 
estimate. Expression for location variance is derived. Section 
I11 compares the estimator’s localization accuracy with the 
CRLB. Performance comparison with those found in the 
literature is presented in Section IV. Section V is a simulation 
study on accuracy of the proposed and the other methods. 
Conclusions are given in Section VI.

(TDOA’s in our case) into groups, each having a size equal 
to the number of unknowns. The unknown parameters are 
computed from each group and then appropriately combined 
to give the final answer. The solution uses stochastic approx- 
imation and requires the Fisher information in each group to 
be sufficiently large. As a consequence, optimum performance 
can be achieved only when the noise is small enough. This 
implies a low noise threshold before performance deviates 
from the C U B . Another difficulty is that if the number of 
sensors is not equal to an integral multiple of the number of 
unknowns plus one, the TDOA estimates from those remaining 
sensors cannot be utilized to improve solution accuracy. 
Our estimator has no such restriction. Moreover, it does not 
require stochastic approximation and hence has a larger noise 
threshold. This is verified by simulations in Section V.

S176.quote:
While the Taylor-series method can give an accurate posi- 
tion estimate at reasonable noise levels, the major drawback is 
that it is iterative, and there is no guarantee for convergence. 
Our approach does not require iteration. If the source is far 
from the array, we compute first the intermediate solution z, 
by (14b) and the final solution by (22b) followed by (24). It 
does not require the computation of 1/r, for i = 1,2, . . , M , 
which is most costly for large M as square root and division 
operations are required. Although computing 1/r, is necessary 
for a near source, it is needed only once. In the Taylor-series 
method, calculation of 1/r, is a must for each iteration as can 
be seen in (7). Finally, no special procedure is required to 
detect divergence.

S177.quote:
Under the condition that the Taylor-series method is prop- 
erly converged, it is of interest to compare the accuracy of 
the two techniques. The Taylor-series method assumes that 
the linearization error is small. It has been illustrated in [17] 
that the higher order terms are significant in determining 
the solution in bad geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) 
situations. Even through the noise power is relatively small, 
there is no guarantee that the obtained solution is accurate. It is 
expected that our method works better in cases where GDOP 
is poor. In fact, our method guarantees optimum performance 
around small TDOA noise region and thus is always be 
superior.

S213.quote:
A new approach for localizing a source from a set of 
hyperbolic curves defined by TDOA measurements is pro- 
posed. By introducing an intermediate variable, the nonlinear 
equations relating TDOA estimates and source position can 
be transformed into a set of equations which are linear 
in the unknown parameters and the intermediate variable. 
A LS then gives their solution. By exploiting the known 
relation between the intermediate variable and the position 
coordinates, a second weighted LS gives the final solution 
for the position coordinates. The covariance matrix of the 
position estimate was derived and found to meet the CRLB. 
The estimator is asymptotically efficient for arbitrary or linear 
array configurations. Indeed, it is an approximation of the ML 
estimator for hyperbolic position fix when the TDOA error is 
small. In the case of a linear array, the solution reduces to 
that of [4]. A comparison with other localization methods was 
conducted. The proposed method has the same simplicity as 
the SI method but performs significantly better, particularly 
when the number of sensors is small. It has a higher noise 
threshold than the DAC method and provides an explicit 
solution form which is not available in existing optimum 
estimators. Finally, the new technique offers a computational 
advantage over the Taylor-series technique and eliminates the 
convergence problem.

concept-9a990bb86d44abbb.title: 到达时间差 (TDOA)
concept-9a990bb86d44abbb.lead: 定位系统的核心观测值
concept-9a990bb86d44abbb.text: 信号到达不同传感器的时间差异。通过广义互相关等方法估计，用于构建描述源位置的双曲线方程。
concept-9a990bb86d44abbb.why: TDOA 是将几何距离差转化为可测量时间的关键，其估计误差直接影响定位精度。

concept-6be8148cccc8a7dd.title: 克拉美 - 罗下界 (CRLB)
concept-6be8148cccc8a7dd.lead: 无偏估计量的方差下限
concept-6be8148cccc8a7dd.text: 理论上任何无偏估计器所能达到的最小方差。本文提出的方法在 small error region（小误差区域）被证明能逼近此下界。
concept-6be8148cccc8a7dd.why: 作为评估定位算法性能的理论基准，用于判断算法是否达到了统计最优。

concept-e3f1e953ec8ce0b5.title: 协方差矩阵 Q
concept-e3f1e953ec8ce0b5.lead: 描述 TDOA 测量误差的相关性与方差
concept-e3f1e953ec8ce0b5.text: 一个 (M-1)×(M-1) 的矩阵，描述了相对于参考传感器的 TDOA 估计误差的统计特性。它取决于信号功率谱 S(w) 和噪声功率谱 N(w)。
concept-e3f1e953ec8ce0b5.why: 在加权最小二乘（WLS）求解中，Q 矩阵用于给不同精度的测量值分配权重，是实现最优估计的关键。

concept-5065db45e0c0e40f.title: 中间变量 r1
concept-5065db45e0c0e40f.lead: 线性化过程中的关键辅助变量
concept-5065db45e0c0e40f.text: 指源到参考传感器（通常为传感器 1）的真实距离。在变换后的线性方程组中，它被视为一个独立的未知数参与求解，最后在第二步中通过几何约束还原其物理意义。
concept-5065db45e0c0e40f.why: 引入 r1 是将非线性问题转化为线性问题的桥梁，使得可以直接使用线性代数工具求解，而无需迭代。

concept-630d317fb340bff0.title: TDOA 噪声模型
concept-630d317fb340bff0.lead: 到达时间差测量中的随机误差建模
concept-630d317fb340bff0.text: 文中假设 TDOA 测量误差在高信噪比下服从渐近正态分布，其协方差结构影响加权最小二乘的权重矩阵设计（R00017）。
concept-630d317fb340bff0.why: 理解噪声统计特性是构建最优估计器的基础，直接影响协方差矩阵 Ψ 的形式。

concept-d0c771c6dba3aef5.title: 广义最小二乘法
concept-d0c771c6dba3aef5.lead: 处理异方差或相关误差的线性回归方法
concept-d0c771c6dba3aef5.text: 当误差项不满足独立同分布时，GLS 通过引入逆协方差矩阵作为权重，使估计量达到最小方差无偏（R00022）。
concept-d0c771c6dba3aef5.why: 本文第一步的核心数学工具，用于在非理想噪声条件下获得更优的初始解。

concept-d4149720e42aee2c.title: 扰动分析
concept-d4149720e42aee2c.lead: 通过线性化研究输入误差对输出估计的影响
concept-d4149720e42aee2c.text: 文中对第一步的估计误差进行一阶泰勒展开，忽略二次及以上项，从而推导第二步误差的统计特性（R00044-R00046）。
concept-d4149720e42aee2c.why: 这是连接两步估计误差协方差的关键数学手段，确保第二步权重矩阵的正确性。

concept-af756ac3830a63b0.title: 最大似然近似
concept-af756ac3830a63b0.lead: 通过分步优化逼近全局最优解
concept-af756ac3830a63b0.text: 作者明确指出两步法是对真实 ML 估计器的近似，因完全联合优化难以解析求解（R00046）。
concept-af756ac3830a63b0.why: 阐明方法本质，避免误认为其为精确最优解。

concept-24a6cd90586b093a.title: 克拉美 - 罗下界 (CRLB)
concept-24a6cd90586b093a.lead: 衡量无偏估计量方差下限的理论基准
concept-24a6cd90586b093a.text: 克拉美 - 罗下界（Cramer-Rao Lower Bound, CRLB）是统计学中用于评估参数估计精度的理论极限。任何无偏估计量的方差都不可能低于 CRLB。若一个估计器的方差达到 CRLB，则称其为有效估计量（efficient estimator）。
concept-24a6cd90586b093a.why: 文中多次提到所提方法在小误差区域能达到 CRLB，表明其在理论上具有最优的估计精度，这是评价该算法性能优越性的核心指标。

concept-0dadd288194b58db.title: 统计有效性
concept-0dadd288194b58db.lead: 估计器方差达到 CRLB 的性质
concept-0dadd288194b58db.text: 文中证明在小误差条件下，所提估计器的协方差矩阵与 CRLB 一致，故在该区域具有统计有效性（R00088, R00093）。
concept-0dadd288194b58db.why: 表明该方法在理想条件下是最优的，为其“高效”标题提供理论支撑。

concept-0b33124a677620e0.title: 矩阵奇异性 (Matrix Singularity)
concept-0b33124a677620e0.lead: 在线性阵列中，传感器位置共线导致几何矩阵秩亏。
concept-0b33124a677620e0.text: 当所有传感器位于同一直线上时，描述位置关系的矩阵行列式为零，不可逆。这会导致最小二乘解无法唯一确定或数值不稳定。
concept-0b33124a677620e0.why: 理解为何通用公式在线性阵列下失效，以及为何需要专门的代数变换。

concept-54097ff1f2aecb88.title: 闭式解 (Closed-Form Solution)
concept-54097ff1f2aecb88.lead: 无需迭代即可直接通过公式计算出的解析解。
concept-54097ff1f2aecb88.text: 本文在线性阵列情况下导出的解是显式的（explicit），不需要像泰勒级数法那样进行迭代搜索，避免了收敛性问题。
concept-54097ff1f2aecb88.why: 强调该方法相对于迭代算法在计算稳定性和速度上的优势。

concept-df4a1a095f136f3a.title: 蒙特卡洛仿真 (Monte Carlo Simulation)
concept-df4a1a095f136f3a.lead: 通过大量重复实验统计评估算法性能的方法。
concept-df4a1a095f136f3a.text: 文中进行了 100,000 次独立运行，每次添加不同的高斯噪声，计算平均 MSE 以消除随机波动，从而可靠地评估估计器的准确性。
concept-df4a1a095f136f3a.why: 解释数据来源的可靠性及 MSE 指标的计算方式。

concept-3b0dc71e718672f0.title: 达到 CRLB (CRLB Attainment)
concept-3b0dc71e718672f0.lead: 估计量的方差达到了理论下限，表示其为有效估计量。
concept-3b0dc71e718672f0.text: 仿真结果显示本文方法的 MSE 与理论计算的 CRLB（表中标记为 E）非常接近，证明该估计量在小误差区域是渐进有效的。
concept-3b0dc71e718672f0.why: 确认算法在统计学意义上的最优性。

concept-0a2d9f8117c000b1.title: 阈值效应 (Threshold Effect)
concept-0a2d9f8117c000b1.lead: 当噪声超过某一临界值时，估计器性能突然急剧恶化的现象。
concept-0a2d9f8117c000b1.text: DAC 方法由于依赖随机近似，仅在发射机位置方差较小时有效。远场源导致位置方差大，因此需要极低的噪声功率才能工作，否则会出现阈值效应。本文方法无此限制。
concept-0a2d9f8117c000b1.why: 解释为何 DAC 方法在远场或高噪声下失效，而本文方法更稳健。

concept-90dee8e705d5f5d5.title: Bhattacharyya 界 (Bhattacharyya Bound)
concept-90dee8e705d5f5d5.lead: 比 CRLB 更紧的理论下界，适用于非线性参数估计和低信噪比情况。
concept-90dee8e705d5f5d5.text: 在低 SNR 下，CRLB 可能过于乐观。Bhattacharyya 界考虑了高阶项，提供了更现实的性能极限。本文方法在低 SNR 下接近 BHB2，表明其接近理论极限。
concept-90dee8e705d5f5d5.why: 提供评估低信噪比下算法性能的更准确基准。

concept-43ecf72f3b1419bd.title: 显式闭式解 (Closed-Form Solution)
concept-43ecf72f3b1419bd.lead: 无需迭代即可直接计算的解析表达式
concept-43ecf72f3b1419bd.text: 闭式解是指可以通过有限次标准数学运算（如加减乘除、开方等）直接得出的解，而不需要借助数值迭代或近似算法。在定位问题中，拥有闭式解意味着可以直接从测量数据计算出目标位置，避免了迭代初值选择和收敛性判断的复杂性。
concept-43ecf72f3b1419bd.why: 本文方法的核心优势之一就是提供了闭式解，这使得它在计算效率和稳定性上优于需要迭代的泰勒级数法，也优于某些无法处理冗余测量的早期闭式解方法。
